name: The Hunchback of Notre Dame
description: The deformed bell-ringer of Notre Dame Cathedral

film.title: The Hunchback of Notre Dame
film.note: Universal built a huge replica of the cathedral's facade on its backlot.

legend: Hugo wrote the novel partly as a protest. In the 1820s Paris was neglecting or tearing down its medieval buildings, and Notre-Dame itself was crumbling. Making the cathedral the true hero of his book, Hugo helped turn public opinion, and in the 1840s the architects Lassus and Viollet-le-Duc began a major restoration. Hugo said the story grew from a Greek word he found carved into a wall of one of the towers: ANANKE, fate.

myths.claim: The cathedral's famous gargoyle-like chimeras were there when Hugo wrote the novel.
myths.explanation: The chimeras on the upper gallery were added during Viollet-le-Duc's 19th-century restoration, after the novel came out.
It is Notre-Dame de Paris. The English translation moved the hunchback to the front.
The great bells he loves so much have taken his hearing.

myths.claim: The novel ends happily for Quasimodo and Esmeralda.
myths.explanation: Esmeralda is executed. Years later, Quasimodo's skeleton is found holding hers in a burial vault.
Its popularity fuelled the campaign that led to the cathedral's 19th-century restoration.

quotes.speaker: An inscription Hugo found carved in the cathedral

powers: Climbs the cathedral like a spider
legacy: The Hunchback of Notre Dame (1939), with Charles Laughton
The Hunchback of Notre Dame (1956), with Anthony Quinn
Disney's The Hunchback of Notre Dame (1996)
facts: Quasimodo is deaf from years of ringing the cathedral bells
He was a foundling, named after Quasimodo Sunday, the day he was found
Hugo's title is Notre-Dame de Paris; the English title put Quasimodo first
The novel helped spur the restoration of Notre-Dame in the 1840s
Many of the cathedral's famous chimeras were added during that restoration
He is fiercely loyal to Esmeralda, who once brought him water at the pillory
Universal built a huge replica of the cathedral's facade for the 1923 film
hostIntro: Ring the bells! Tonight's guest lives high above Paris and has the best view in town. He can't hear you clapping, so clap twice as hard.
